summary: Smita Halder is an Indology and history and archaeology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Susmita Basu Majumdar. As of 2026, she is attested as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

So Takahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo. He served at Meijo University as an associate professor (attested 1977–1978) and professor (attested 1991).

Sodo Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned degrees from Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Kogen Mizuno and Hajime Nakamura. His career included professorships at Josai University and Aichi Gakuin University (1991–2003).
Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar. He studied at Antai-ji (1949–1957) under Kodo Sawaki, as well as under Ekō Hashimoto, and taught Joko Shibata.

Soen Nakagawa (1907–1984) was a Buddhist studies figure who attended the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo, studying traditionally under Gempo Yamamoto. He taught numerous students, including Robert Baker Aitken, Philip Kapleau, and Maurine Stuart.

Sogaku Harada (1871–1961) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University under teachers including Sotan Oka and Dokutan Sōsan. He served as a professor at Komazawa University from 1911 to 1923.
Sogen Asahina (1891–1979) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who was educated at Nihon University. He taught Koun Yamada and Kyozo Yamada and held a post at Kanagawa University.

Sogen Omori (1904–1994) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Nihon University. He became abbot of Koho-in in 1947, was appointed professor at Hanazono University in 1970, and served as its president from 1978 to 1982.

Sogyal Rinpoche (1947–2019) worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, studying at the University of Delhi, the University of Cambridge, and under several traditional masters. He founded Rigpa in 1975.

Soiku Shigematsu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. He taught at Shizuoka Women's University, Shizuoka University (1975–2001), and Kansai Medical University (2001–2006).

Sojo Hirano (1928–2007) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an associate professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and as shike at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996). He taught Sonja Arntzen and Yoel Hoffmann.

Sokatsu Shaku (1870–1954) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Kōsen Imakita and Soyen Shaku. He founded Ryobokai (1901), the Ryobokai Dojo of North America (1906), and Ningen Zen, and taught Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki.

Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki (1882–1945) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied art in Tokyo and California, as well as under Sokatsu Shaku and Soyen Shaku. He founded the First Zen Institute of America in 1930.

Sokichi Tsuda (1873–1961) was a scholar of history, sinology, and japanology who studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō. He held posts at the SMR Research Department, Waseda University (where he also founded an entity in 1935), and the University of Tokyo.

Soko Morinaga (1925–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyama High School and Daitoku-ji under Sesso Oda and Zuigan Goto. He served as abbot of Daishuin (~1963–1995) and head of Hanazono University (1986–1994).

Sokuo Eto (1888–1958) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Komazawa University, the University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. He served as president of Komazawa Junior College (~1950–1958) and as a professor at Komazawa University.

Solomon George FitzHerbert is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford. He served as Departmental Lecturer at Oxford and as a researcher at the National Centre for Scientific Research (attested 2019).
Soma Thera (1898–1960) was a Buddhist studies figure educated at St. Benedict's College, Colombo. He studied under Jetavana Sayadaw in 1936 and was a member of Servants of the Buddha (~1928–1936).

Somadeva Vasudeva is an Indologist who earned a PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He has held positions at the French Institute of Pondicherry, Columbia University as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit, and Kyoto University as a visiting scholar.

Somboon Watana is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who received a PhD from Panjab University in 1999 under Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma. He serves as an Assistant Professor at Mahidol University (attested 2026).
